title: One List Of States
eyebrow: The two new states now reach every part of the board, and a second list cannot be added

actions.fyi: Nothing is waiting on you. This is the fix to what you spotted in the state menu.

content.label: What you spotted, and how far it went
content.lead: The menu was one of nine places that had never heard of the two new states.

blocks.text: A card waiting on you, or a cancelled one, was being dropped from the counts entirely — the ring on the project tile could not add up to the board.

rows.title: You can send a card to your own column, and drop one
rows.note: Both were columns you could look at but never put a card into. Choosing Cancelled does what the board does underneath — finishes the card and marks it dropped — rather than writing a word the board would refuse.

rows.title: A state is declared once
rows.note: Its name, its column heading, its colour, its icon and its keyboard shortcut are one line in one file. Adding a seventh state is that one line.

rows.title: A second list cannot appear quietly
rows.note: Three state names inside six lines of any other file is a copy of the list, and the check goes red naming the file. Shown by putting the old four-entry menu back: it named the menu.

content.label: Checked on the running board
content.lead: Read out of a real browser pointed at the board you are looking at, not from the code.

blocks.text: The same check now opens a card and refuses if the state menu cannot set a state the board draws a column for: six columns, six entries.

items: 99 checks on the screen's side are green, 7 of them new and about the list itself.
309 checks on the server's side are green, including the two new numbers it keeps.
Putting the old four-entry menu back turns the guard red and names the file it is in.
Adding a seventh state without telling the server turns it red too, because those cards would vanish from the counts.

decisions.title: The list lives with the screen, and the server is held to it rather than given a copy
decisions.why: The server is written in another language and cannot read the list. It counts state by state, so a check fails when a state exists that it has never heard of.

decisions.title: Choosing Cancelled finishes the card and marks it, instead of writing the word
decisions.why: The board has no such state to write; dropped work is a finished card carrying a mark. A menu entry that cannot be set is worse than one that is missing.

decisions.title: The colours are spelled out once per colour, not built from the state's name
decisions.why: The styling tool only ships a colour it can read as a literal word, so a built-up name renders grey. The list still decides which colour each state gets.

decisions.title: A rule that a job's state follows the work under it now matches on both sides
decisions.why: The screen and the server had drifted into two different rules for the same question. They now use the same order.

next.if_nothing: Nothing. This is live on your board now.
